sections.h2: What are my options for selling a house fast in Horizon City?
sections.html:
A Horizon City owner can sell through an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer. Most of the town is owner-occupied: the Census Bureau reports 85.2% of homes are lived in by their owners, so many sellers are families who bought a house to stay in.

With that many owners, a typical sale here is a family house. A cash offer fits when you need a firm closing date or do not want to spend on repairs. A listing fits when the house is in good shape and you can wait for a buyer who needs a loan.

  • Gather your deed, the latest tax statement and any HOA or utility district paperwork.
  • Ask for any offer in writing, with the closing date and who pays which costs.
  • Confirm the buyer can show funds before you take the house off the market.

sections.h2: Where is Horizon City and how did it start?
sections.html:
Horizon City is a town in El Paso County, about 15 miles east of the city of El Paso on the Hueco Bolson, according to the town's comprehensive plan. The Franklin Mountains lie to the west and Mexico about 20 miles to the south. The plan puts the elevation at 4,022 feet, the average annual rainfall near 7.77 inches, and the July average high at 94 degrees Fahrenheit.

The same plan says a Chicago-based developer announced the project in December 1959, and that a planning organization from Tucson laid out the town alongside the proposed route of Interstate 10. The first home sold on October 31, 1962, and growth stayed slow through the 1960s, with about 94 occupied homes by 1971. The town incorporated on August 13, 1988, and voters approved its charter in November 1997. It is a home rule city with a mayor and a seven-member council.

The desert setting shapes a house in practical ways. Dry air and strong sun are hard on roofs, stucco and exterior paint, and a buyer's inspector will look at cooling equipment and the roof. Fix cheap items before listing, or price the house to reflect them.

sections.h2: What does Census data say about Horizon City housing?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows a median home value of $170,200 for 2020 to 2024, and a population of 25,118 in 2025, up 11.8% from the 2020 base. Growth at that pace keeps new subdivisions coming, so your house competes with new construction.

sections.h2: Which schools and local offices matter when selling in Horizon City?
sections.html:
The town's plan names two school districts, the Socorro and Clint Independent School Districts, and a Horizon Regional Municipal Utility District among the local agencies it consulted. Which district serves your address is a fact buyers ask about, so look it up on your tax bill or ask the appraisal district.

The El Paso Central Appraisal District values all real and business personal property in El Paso County. Its home page lists protests and appeals, exemption forms, a deadline calendar and a taxpayer liaison who helps with complaints about the review board. Under the state calendar, a protest is due by May 15, or 30 days after you get your notice if that is later.

  • Appraisal district: value, exemptions and protests.
  • County tax office: the bill and a statement of what is owed.
  • County clerk: the deed and other recorded papers.
  • Town hall: permits, zoning questions and utility accounts.

sections.h2: How does Texas record a deed and handle recording fees?
sections.html:
The deed goes to the El Paso County Clerk, who acts as the county recorder. To be recorded, the instrument has to be signed and acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer, or sworn before two witnesses.

The Texas Courts clerk manual from 2023 lists a $5.00 charge for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus $0.25 for each name over five that must be indexed. It also lists extra records fees, such as a records technology fee of $2.00 and management and archive fees capped at $10 each. A missing mailing address for the grantee can add $25. The county can change these, so ask the clerk for the current schedule.

Your title company usually handles the filing. The deed must go in the county where the property sits, so a Horizon City house is recorded in El Paso County.

sections.h2: What happens if taxes are unpaid or a lien is on the house?
sections.html:
The tax lien attaches on January 1 each year and stays with the property, not the person who owned it. The Comptroller says the lien lets a court order the property foreclosed and sold even after ownership changed, and a buyer cannot get clear title until the delinquent taxes are paid.

Taxes unpaid after January 31 are delinquent. Penalty and interest start on February 1, and a unit's collection attorney may add a further charge. If a house is sold at a tax sale, the Texas Supreme Court describes a redemption right: homestead, farm and mineral property can be redeemed for two years after the purchaser's deed is filed, at a premium of 25 percent in year one and 50 percent in year two, and other property for 180 days.

The State Law Library adds that a former owner has two years to claim excess proceeds from a tax foreclosure sale. If you are behind, selling before a suit is filed avoids added court costs. Ask the tax office for a payoff figure, and ask whether an installment plan is available, which some collectors offer for a residence homestead.

sections.h2: Does Horizon City have rules on building or renting?
sections.html:
The town runs a Planning and Zoning Commission and a Board of Adjustment that advise the council on zoning and development, and a seller who added a room, fence or carport should ask town hall whether it was permitted. A buyer's lender and title company may ask.

If you rent the house, you also need to give notice under the lease before the property changes hands. A tenant who stays after notice can lead to an eviction case in justice court, and Texas requires at least three days' written notice to vacate unless the lease says otherwise. A cash buyer will often take a house with a tenant in place, but that changes the price and the timeline.

faqs.q: How many people live in Horizon City?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 25,118 residents as of July 1, 2025. That is 11.8% above the April 2020 base of 22,461.

faqs.q: Do I pay a transfer tax to sell in Horizon City?
faqs.a: The county clerk manual lists recording fees and says nothing of a transfer tax. Ask your title company for the full settlement statement, which shows every charge on your side.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Horizon City house with unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, but the taxes must be paid at or before closing. The tax lien follows the house, so the title company will not clear title until the delinquent amount is settled. Request a payoff statement from the county tax office.
The El Paso Central Appraisal District. It values property as of January 1, and you can protest by May 15 or within 30 days of the notice, whichever is later.

faqs.q: Is the house worth more because of its location?
faqs.a: Location counts, since commute and highway access matter to buyers here. The Census median of $170,200 is a citywide figure, so get a written offer or an appraisal for your own address.
